feed.title: Databases — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: A hand-curated, annotated link directory across ten areas, from software and AI to security, economics and architecture. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: PostgreSQLCO.NF
entry.content:
Searchable documentation for every postgresql.conf parameter, with version differences, defaults and community recommendations. Unlike the official manual it adds per-parameter tuning advice and context.

https://postgresqlco.nf/doc/en/param/

entry.title: Select Star SQL
entry.content:
An interactive online book that teaches SQL through exercises run in the browser against one real dataset. Unlike syntax references it builds query reasoning step by step around a single dataset's story.

https://selectstarsql.com/

entry.title: Awesome DB Tools
entry.content:
A list of tools that make working with databases easier (clients, migration, schema). Unlike single-database lists it looks at engine-agnostic helper tools.

https://github.com/mgramin/awesome-db-tools

entry.title: Awesome MongoDB
entry.content:
A list of libraries and tools for MongoDB, the document-based NoSQL database. Unlike general NoSQL lists it focuses on one product’s driver and ODM ecosystem.

https://github.com/ramnes/awesome-mongodb

entry.title: Awesome Postgres
entry.content:
A list of extensions, tools and resources for PostgreSQL. Unlike the official docs it shows the ecosystem’s extensions and management tools together.

https://github.com/dhamaniasad/awesome-postgres

entry.title: Beekeeper Studio
entry.content:
An open-source SQL editor and manager supporting many databases. Compared with DBeaver its interface is simpler and more modern, with fewer advanced features in exchange.

https://www.beekeeperstudio.io/

entry.title: CockroachDB
entry.content:
A distributed SQL database that scales horizontally with strong consistency and survivability, speaking the PostgreSQL protocol. Unlike single-node PostgreSQL it replicates across regions; since 2024 it has no open-source core and is offered free to individuals, students and businesses under $10M annual revenue under an enterprise licence.

https://www.cockroachlabs.com

entry.title: ConnectionStrings.com
entry.content:
A reference giving the correct connection-string format for every database and driver. Unlike hunting the docs it gathers the syntax of dozens of drivers in one place.

https://www.connectionstrings.com/

entry.title: dbdiagram.io
entry.content:
A tool that turns a simple text DSL (DBML) into shareable ER diagrams fast. Unlike drag-and-drop diagram tools you type the schema — no aligning boxes by hand — and can export it to SQL.

https://dbdiagram.io

entry.title: DBeaver
entry.content:
A universal desktop database client managing many databases from one interface. Compared with Beekeeper Studio it is far more comprehensive — ER diagrams, data transfer, hundreds of drivers — but Java-based and heavy.

https://dbeaver.io

entry.title: MariaDB
entry.content:
A community-driven open-source fork of MySQL, usable as a drop-in replacement.

https://mariadb.org

entry.title: Modern SQL
entry.content:
Markus Winand’s site teaching modern SQL features such as window functions across dialects. Unlike general SQL tutorials, it tabulates which databases support each feature and since which version.

https://modern-sql.com

entry.title: Neon
entry.content:
Serverless Postgres with branching and scale-to-zero; it joined Databricks in 2025. Unlike traditional managed Postgres you can branch the database like git — an instant copy for every PR.

https://neon.tech

entry.title: PlanetScale
entry.content:
Serverless MySQL built on Vitess, managing schema changes through branches with no downtime. Unlike classic managed MySQL it offers that branching and non-blocking migrations; its free tier was removed in 2024.

https://planetscale.com

entry.title: PostgreSQL Exercises
entry.content:
Practise SQL with graded PostgreSQL exercises in the browser. Compared with SQLBolt it is PostgreSQL-specific and more advanced, including recursive queries and window functions.

https://pgexercises.com

entry.title: Redis Insight
entry.content:
Redis’s official GUI — browse, edit, query and profile your data. Instead of third-party tools such as RESP.app (RedisDesktopManager), this is now the official option.

https://redis.io/insight/

entry.title: SQLBolt
entry.content:
Interactive SQL lessons that teach by doing in the browser; each lesson ends with an exercise where you write the query. Unlike video courses you write queries instead of watching; it sits at a more basic level than PostgreSQL tutorials.

https://sqlbolt.com

entry.title: SurrealDB
entry.content:
A multi-model database combining document, graph and relational in one engine. Instead of running a document store, a graph database and a SQL database separately, you use them all through one query language — at the cost of less maturity than established databases.

https://surrealdb.com

entry.title: Use The Index, Luke!
entry.content:
Markus Winand’s developer-focused guide to SQL indexing and performance. Unlike general SQL books, it focuses solely on indexing and compares every topic across five major databases.

https://use-the-index-luke.com

entry.title: Turso
entry.content:
A database platform built on libSQL, a SQLite fork, that replicates the database to edge nodes near the user. Unlike centralised services such as PlanetScale, read latency becomes local file access rather than a network round trip.

https://turso.tech/

entry.title: Oracle SQL Developer
entry.content:
A free desktop client for Oracle databases combining querying, schema browsing and PL/SQL debugging. Unlike general clients such as DBeaver it has a PL/SQL debugger and Oracle-specific tooling — the usual tool if you work with Oracle.

https://www.oracle.com/database/sqldeveloper/

entry.title: PocketBase
entry.content:
A backend shipping as one Go file, providing SQLite, auth and a real-time API. Unlike heavy stacks it reduces the server to a single executable.

https://pocketbase.io/

entry.title: SQLite
entry.content:
A serverless embedded database living in a single file — the most widely deployed database engine in the world. Unlike server databases such as PostgreSQL it needs no separate process or setup; its test coverage is legendary.

https://sqlite.org/

entry.title: SQLZoo
entry.content:
An exercise set that teaches SQL by making you write queries in the browser, each section over its own dataset. That is the difference from tutorials needing an install: your first `SELECT` requires no database.

https://sqlzoo.net/wiki/SQL_Tutorial

entry.title: Supabase
entry.content:
An open-source Firebase alternative adding auth, APIs and storage on top of Postgres. Unlike Firebase it stands on relational Postgres and can be self-hosted.

https://supabase.com/

entry.title: Couchbase Learn
entry.content:
Queries a document store with a SQL-like language (N1QL), which is a gentler break for teams arriving from the relational world than MongoDB’s query syntax.

https://learn.couchbase.com/learn

entry.title: Firebase
entry.content:
Realtime database, auth, storage and hosting in one package. Unlike Supabase it is NoSQL: it accelerates a prototype sharply, while query flexibility and vendor lock-in become the later problem.

https://firebase.google.com/docs

entry.title: MongoDB University
entry.content:
MongoDB’s official free courses. Unlike third-party courses it puts weight on data modelling — designing a document store with relational habits is the most common source of performance trouble.

https://learn.mongodb.com/

entry.title: MySQL Tutorial
entry.content:
Works MySQL end to end over a sample database, treating join types, subqueries and stored procedures separately. Far more readable as an introduction than the official manual.

https://www.mysqltutorial.org/

entry.title: PostgreSQL Tutorial
entry.content:
A PostgreSQL tutorial showing each topic with a runnable query. Unlike most SQL courses, it goes deep on window functions and CTEs.

https://neon.com/postgresql/tutorial

entry.title: İlişkisel Veritabanı Tasarımı
entry.content:
A full course on normal forms and schema design. It teaches getting the tables right rather than writing queries — which is where every later problem originates.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=26ls5lNiijk

entry.title: Veritabanları Derinlemesine
entry.content:
A course on internals — index structures, transaction isolation levels, locking. Not a product tutorial; it holds regardless of which database you use.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pPqazMTzNOM

entry.title: SQL Sıfırdan İleri Seviye
entry.content:
SQL from basics to advanced in four hours for anyone who wants the whole picture in one sitting. It reaches window functions rather than stopping at basic SELECT.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OT1RErkfLNQ
